thread:
oliver: Quick question for release flow: how do we want to treat tiny hotfixes that are purely config/ops toggles vs behavior/API fixes? Do we always bump the patch, or can we rely on prerelease/build metadata for internal churn?

sylvia: my instinct is patch bump for anything that affects customers or any API/behavior semantics. makes pins simple. :+1: 

aj: semver note: build metadata (e.g. 1.22.7+build.20260320) does NOT affect precedence. prerelease (1.22.7-canary.20260320) is lower than released 1.22.7. So if you want package managers to consider it "newer", you must bump patch to 1.22.8.

maria: proposal: reserve patch bumps for public fixes. for internal/ops-only toggles use prerelease/canary tags with date so deploy-bot can auto-route. release notes get flagged as internal.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy: tag=1.22.7-canary.20260320 -> pool=canaries, pct=15, region=us-east-1. ETA ~8m.

noah: quick example: toggling telemetry sampling from 0.1 -> 0.05 is ops-only. i'd prefer not to churn patch numbers for those.

aj: agreed for opt-in ops changes. BUT if we need downstream customers pinned to exact-version to pick the change, that's not visible unless we bump patch. exact-pinned customers won't get prerelease/build metadata.

ops-jenna: operational ask: when a patch tag is pushed, deploy-bot should auto-create a release draft with a rollback-playbook pointer and checklist. example tagging flow we use locally:

```
# create a hotfix
git checkout -b hotfix/kv-cache-drop
git commit -m "hotfix: fix kv cache null path"
git tag -a 1.22.8 -m "hotfix: fix kv cache drop"
git push origin 1.22.8
```

maria: release-bot rule: if tag matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-patch\d+)?$/ then create public draft. if tag includes "-canary." or "+build" then mark release internal and don't attach to public change log.

release-bot: Draft release created: "1.22.8" (#312). Attached auto-generated rollback playbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/rollback-playbook. Marked backports: agent-runtime, kv-cache.

oliver: TL;DR decision:
- Behavioral/API/backported bugfix -> bump patch (x.y.(z+1)) and create public release.
- Config/ops-only -> use prerelease or build metadata (x.y.z-canary.YYYYMMDD or x.y.z+build.sha) and keep internal unless explicitly requested.
- deploy-bot: auto-schedule canaries for "-canary." tags and auto-draft public releases for strictly numeric patch tags.

aj: I'll add a small section to the release docs about semver precedence and the exact-match pin gotcha.

maria: i'll update the release checklist template with a "behavioral change?" checkbox so authors don't forget.

sylvia: nice. also we should add a short note for on-call: prerelease tags are safe to rollback with last stable patch; patch tags need a proper rollback playbook. saves time during incidents.

oliver: thanks all. we'll codify this in the release docs and add deploy-bot hooks for the draft scaffold.

deploy-bot: canary started: 1.22.7-canary.20260320 -> healthy: 5/5 hosts.

release-bot: reminder: link to changelog shall include "internal" label for canary drafts.

maria: will follow up with the PR updating the docs and the release template.

oliver: tagging docs owners: @aj for semantics, @maria & @ops-jenna for automation. closing this thread unless objections. :white_check_mark:
